newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sweet crude grades advance on Brent arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sweet crude grades advance on Brent arbitrage.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices saw morning gains halved by Tuesday afternoon on a pullback in the NYMEX futures market, but traders said the session's main feature was the strength in sweet grade barrels.
Deals were recorded for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at discounts of 24 cents to the West Texas Intermediate/Cushing in the morning, to later trades at WTI/Cushing -19 cents.

Both the morning and afternoon LLS trades marked an advance from the price levels dealt on Monday. Cash dealers said a closed arbitrage for bringing North Sea Brent barrels to the U.S. Gulf bolstered LLS.
"The arbitrage for Brent is closed enough. It looks like prompt barrels are finding a little support from the fact Brent is not fixed to come over here," said a U.S. trader.
Benchmark July WTI/Cushing was currently talked at $18.95-19.05 a barrel, around 10 cents firmer than late Monday, and 20 cents over the July NYMEX price range at $18.75-85 a barrel.
Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) remained set at a 20 cents premium to the paper value, traders noted.

Other grade talk had West Texas Sour/Midland sold at a $1.65 discount to the marker, around five cents stronger than deals late Monday. Signs of strength in the Urals market aided the sour performance, but overall traders said fundamentals were firmly on the bearish side for heavier grades.
In general, market players said there were no refiners buying crude for storage. "Why would you buy something now when five days later you could save 20 cents," said a trader.

Outright crudes were waiting for tonight's American Petroleum Institute (API) report for market direction. A Reuters survey showed wide expectations for crude inventories, balancing around the unchanged level, while distillates were seen building by an average of 2.5 million barrels and gasoline stocks adding around 1.1 million barrels.
Refinery utilization rates were forecast to ease from the extremely high 98.4 percent level recorded in last week's API measurement.
